cookbooks.md.title: Cookbooks
cookbooks.md.description: End-to-end recipes that show TypeSafe in real problems, from a few questions to full pipelines.

cookbooks/autoformat.md.title: Structure recovery
cookbooks/autoformat.md.description: Reconstructs Markdown from plain text that lost its formatting in two requests: one stitches hard-wrapped lines back together, one classifies every block (heading, list, code, callout).

cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.title: Autoresearch feature discovery
cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.description: Let an LLM propose questions about labelled text, have Jev answer them for every row, and train CatBoost on the answers, feeding its misses back to the next step. The worked example predicts how polite Wikipedia editors' requests read.

cookbooks/basic_memory.md.title: Simple memory system
cookbooks/basic_memory.md.description: Let Jev decide which requests and answers are worth remembering, then wrap the Jev call in a small function that adds memories to later calls.

cookbooks/cart_from_primitives.md.title: Shopping cart
cookbooks/cart_from_primitives.md.description: Turns a natural-language cafe order into a structured cart: a shrinking-options loop of Choice questions finds every item, then one batched request per item fills its known fields.

cookbooks/citation_check.md.title: Double-checking citations
cookbooks/citation_check.md.description: Catch wrong or hallucinated citations by checking against the source document. One Choice question decides whether the quote's context supports the claim.

cookbooks/classification_using_confidenc.title: Classification using confidence
cookbooks/classification_using_confidenc.description: Classify SEC annual reports into 75 industry groups with one Choice each, then read the answer's own confidence to decide whether to report that group or the broader division above it.

cookbooks/classifying_rag_passages.md.title: Classifying RAG passages
cookbooks/classifying_rag_passages.md.description: Score each retrieved passage with one TypeSafe request, then decide in code which ones reach the answering model.

cookbooks/consistency_choice_cookbook.md.title: Self-consistency: choices
cookbooks/consistency_choice_cookbook.md.description: Ask a model the same moderation question twice: how often does the decision change? A test of reliability that needs no answer key, comparing LLMs and Jev on borderline posts.

cookbooks/consistency_noul_cookbook.md.title: Self-consistency: nouls
cookbooks/consistency_noul_cookbook.md.description: Ask a model about the same insurance claim twice: how often does the decision change? A test of reliability that needs no answer key, comparing LLMs and Jev on borderline claims.

cookbooks/date_extraction_cookbook.md.title: Date extraction
cookbooks/date_extraction_cookbook.md.description: Extracts absolute and relative dates by asking Jev for the parts named in a document, then resolving and validating them in code with confidence-based review.

cookbooks/entity_alignment.md.title: Knowledge graph entity alignment
cookbooks/entity_alignment.md.description: Route candidate record pairs from two sources to a merge recommendation, manual review, or no link, using one Score question. Three Noul questions check individual fields. The worked example uses 450 album pairs from Wikidata and MusicBrainz.

cookbooks/feeder_watch.md.title: Feeder-cam visit log
cookbooks/feeder_watch.md.description: Send frames from bird feeder camera footage to Jev with five questions, one of them a Box that finds the bird, then use plain code to turn the answers into a visit log per species.

cookbooks/function_calling.md.title: Function calling
cookbooks/function_calling.md.description: Turns natural-language trading requests into calls to ordinary typed functions by mapping function names and closed-set arguments to confidence-aware System One questions.

cookbooks/hierarchical_classification.md.title: Hierarchical classification
cookbooks/hierarchical_classification.md.description: Uses parallel beam search over Jev's Choice probabilities to classify documents in deep patent, retail product, and biomedical hierarchies.

cookbooks/infinite_cardinality_choice.md.title: Infinite cardinality choice
cookbooks/infinite_cardinality_choice.md.description: From someone's own description, find the film they half-remember among 5,000: one Noul per film on a short plot, again on a long plot for the top eighty, and one Choice over the top twenty. The right film comes first 78% of the time, against 33% when embedding search builds the shortlist.

cookbooks/intelliprompter.md.title: Intelliprompter
cookbooks/intelliprompter.md.description: Tick off a presenter's notes as they speak: Jev scores the live transcript against each note not yet covered, and a note stays ticked once its score passes the threshold.

cookbooks/llm_guardrails.md.title: Guardrails for LLMs
cookbooks/llm_guardrails.md.description: Screens every message into and out of an LLM app with one TypeSafe request, then passes, reviews, blocks, or sends it to support by thresholds you set.

cookbooks/ocr_confidence_bounding_boxes..title: OCR confidence and bounding boxes
cookbooks/ocr_confidence_bounding_boxes..description: Check the values an OCR extractor read from invoice photos: Jev boxes each value, scores it against the page and against a crop of its box, and flags low scores for review.

cookbooks/parallel_questions.md.title: Parallel questions
cookbooks/parallel_questions.md.description: Runs a 13-question regulatory briefing over the GDPR Wikipedia article, showing that batching every question into one TypeSafe call is 12.2x cheaper and 11.8x faster with no change in answers.

cookbooks/pre_parsed_value_extraction_co.title: Pre-parsed value extraction
cookbooks/pre_parsed_value_extraction_co.description: Finds candidate emails, phone numbers, and amounts with a regex, has Jev pick the one you ask for, and normalizes that exact span in code.

cookbooks/reading_scanned_documents.md.title: Reading a scanned vaccination record
cookbooks/reading_scanned_documents.md.description: Find each vaccine on a scanned travel record with a Noul and a Box, read the year of each dose with a Choice that can answer unreadable, and check each dose still covers the trip in a text-only request.

cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md.title: Re-ranking
cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md.description: Builds 30-passage BM25 shortlists for 40 CLERC legal queries, then uses one System One question per query-candidate pair to raise top-1 accuracy from 5% to 30% and top-10 accuracy from 38% to 65%.

cookbooks/sde_cascade.md.title: SDE cascade
cookbooks/sde_cascade.md.description: Extracts structured data with a cheap model, checks each field with Jev, and escalates to a reasoning model only when a check fires.

cookbooks/semantic_find.md.title: Line-by-line search
cookbooks/semantic_find.md.description: Build semantic search for GitHub's Terms of Service. In one request, score 218 line ids against a plain-language query with a Choice question, and use a Noul question to check whether the document contains an answer.

cookbooks/skill_suggestion.md.title: Skill suggestion
cookbooks/skill_suggestion.md.description: Picks at most one skill for an agent turn out of the 194 in Nous Research's Hermes catalog, using two TypeSafe requests to rank and re-check the top candidates.

cookbooks/twitch_chat_filter.md.title: Twitch chat filter
cookbooks/twitch_chat_filter.md.description: Hides insults, spam, and unasked-for gameplay tips in Twitch chat, blurs spoilers, and highlights questions. Each message gets one TypeSafe request with three questions, requests run concurrently, and plain rules in code turn the answers into what the viewer sees.

cookbooks/verify_llm_outputs.md.title: Verifying LLM answers against their source
cookbooks/verify_llm_outputs.md.description: Check whether an LLM's answer follows from the paragraphs it was given, using three Noul questions in one request, and send the doubtful answers to review.

demos.md.title: Made with Jev
demos.md.description: Working projects built on Jev, and how each one works.

demos/airbnb-listing-search.md.title: Airbnb listing search in Google Sheets
demos/airbnb-listing-search.md.description: Describe a stay in plain English and get the 10 best of 1,000 Cape Town Airbnb listings, scored out of 10, in about a second, from a formula in Google Sheets.

demos/content-audit.md.title: Content audits with Jev
demos/content-audit.md.description: Audit all of the Django documentation in under 5 seconds for $0.10. Get an overview of what kind of content you have, what needs fixing, and where to spend effort.

demos/smart-home.md.title: Smart home assistant demo
demos/smart-home.md.description: Demo code: a smart home assistant that uses Jev to evaluate user requests.

images.md.title: Images
images.md.description: Send images in a System One request: in the state, inside a question's instructions, and as the criteria a question is judged against.

introduction.md.title: Introduction
introduction.md.description: Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first System One model. Send state and typed questions; get structured answers your code can use directly.

introduction/coding-agents.md.title: Jev with coding agents
introduction/coding-agents.md.description: What Jev is (and isn't) when you're using a coding agent.

introduction/machine-learning-primer.md.title: AI primer
introduction/machine-learning-primer.md.description: Why TypeSafe trains decision models with calibrated probabilities instead of optimizing for generated text.

model-jaggedness.md.title: Model jaggedness
model-jaggedness.md.description: Jev isn't perfect. Here are some jagged edges we are aware of. Many of these will be fixed in later versions.

model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md.title: Jev 1.13 jaggedness
model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md.description: Jev isn't perfect. Here are some jagged edges we are aware of with jev-1.13. Many of these will be fixed in later versions.

patterns.md.title: Patterns
patterns.md.description: Architectural patterns for building systems with TypeSafe.

patterns/companion-noul.md.title: Companion Noul
patterns/companion-noul.md.description: Pair a Choice with a Noul that asks whether any option fits, so your code can tell when none does.

patterns/composite-scoring.md.title: Composite scoring
patterns/composite-scoring.md.description: Break a complex judgment into atomic scores, combine with weights you control in code.

patterns/confidence-routing.md.title: Routing by confidence
patterns/confidence-routing.md.description: Use confidence as a second axis. The score tells you what; confidence tells you whether to act on it.

patterns/fan-out.md.title: Speculative fan-out
patterns/fan-out.md.description: Send many questions in a single request, including speculative ones, and let your code decide what's relevant.

patterns/intent-routing.md.title: Intent routing
patterns/intent-routing.md.description: Classify incoming requests and route each to the optimal handler: deterministic logic, a specialist LLM, or a human.

patterns/noul-screen.md.title: Screen with a Noul first
patterns/noul-screen.md.description: Ask one yes/no question first, and run the expensive step only when the answer is a clear yes.

patterns/probability-routing.md.title: Routing by probability
patterns/probability-routing.md.description: Give riskier actions a higher probability threshold. The answer says what to do, and its probability says whether to do it.

primitives.md.title: Primitives (Questions)
primitives.md.description: The System One question types, the typed answers they return, how to choose between them, and how to ask several at once.

primitives/advanced.md.title: Advanced: structure
primitives/advanced.md.description: Instructions, Choice options, Score levels, and Noul criteria all accept JSON structure.

primitives/box.md.title: Box
primitives/box.md.description: A Box is a System One question type for finding where something is in an image. The answer is the four edges of a box around it, as fractions of the image's width and height.

primitives/choice.md.title: Choice
primitives/choice.md.description: A Choice is a System One question type for selecting one option from a defined set. The answer includes the selected option, a probability for each option, and confidence.

primitives/noul.md.title: Noul
primitives/noul.md.description: A Noul question asks Jev to evaluate a yes/no question and return the probability that the answer is yes.

primitives/score.md.title: Score
primitives/score.md.description: A Score is a System One question type for rating content against ordered, descriptive levels. The answer includes a score, a probability for each level, and confidence.
